text:
Fifteen shooters had tried and failed. Macklin Celebrini, Bo Horvat, Matthew Schaefer, all of them. Then Ivar Stenberg came in as the 16th shooter of the shootout, scored, and San Jose had its first win in six games, 3-2 over the Islanders, ending a 0-5-0 run. Somewhere in the sixth round NHL.com's Stefen Rosner posted "Dickinson stopped by Sorokin. This is madness," which covers it.

The regulation part had its own small story. Ben Hutton, signed to a one-year deal last week as injuries thinned the Islanders' blue line (Ryan Pulock is out two to four weeks, per Daily Faceoff), opened the scoring at 6:14. San Jose owned the first period on expected goals, the quality of the chances, 1.08 to 0.49, and Stenberg tipped one in at 16:41 to tie it. Victor Eklund's power-play slap shot 1:11 into the second pushed New York's win chance from 51 to 68 percent, and Tyler Toffoli answered with a slap shot of his own at 12:12. That goal was the biggest swing of the night, taking the Sharks from 31 to 52 percent, and Toffoli did it in 10:54 of ice time.

After that it belonged to the goalies. Ilya Sorokin stopped 37 of 39 and saved 2.12 goals more than the shots deserved, best of all a 34 percent look from Celebrini in overtime. By our wins-added count he did more to win this game than anyone, 0.71, and lost it anyway. "Sorokin brilliant. Didn't get what he deserved for a second straight game," Rosner wrote. Yaroslav Askarov was the first star at the other end, 30 saves on 32 shots and 1.29 goals saved above expected.

The Sharks earned this one. They led in expected goals 4.12 to 3.29 and in shot attempts 68 to 56, and won 62 percent of our replays of every shot. For a team that has spent a week losing, that matters. The Islanders take a point but are winless in four (0-2-2), with Schaefer logging 30:54 and the shootout leaving them where the week found them.
headline: Stenberg ends a 15-miss shootout and a Sharks skid
